dialogue.speaker: Julieta
dialogue.spanish: Che, Tomás, mirá el cartel en la escalera: la línea D del subte está cortada por obras.
dialogue.english: Hey, Tomás, look at the sign on the stairs: subway Line D is closed for maintenance.

slang.actualMeaning: the Buenos Aires subway / metro system
slang.example: Tomamos el subte en Plaza Italia para llegar rápido al centro.

dialogue.speaker: Tomás
dialogue.spanish: ¡Uh, qué garrón! Y encima me parece que no tengo nada de saldo en la tarjeta SUBE para el colectivo.
dialogue.english: Ugh, what a bummer! And on top of that I don't think I have any balance on my SUBE card for the bus.

slang.actualMeaning: what a total bummer / drag / bad luck (Argentine slang)
slang.example: ¡Qué garrón que se largó a llover justo ahora!

dialogue.speaker: Julieta
dialogue.spanish: Bueno, tranquilo, boludo, acá a media cuadra sobre Santa Fe hay un kiosco abierto donde cargan saldo.
dialogue.english: Well, relax, dude, half a block from here on Santa Fe Avenue there's an open kiosk where they load balance.

slang.actualMeaning: dude / buddy (friendly everyday Argentine address between close friends)
slang.example: Che, boludo, ¿a qué hora nos encontramos hoy?

dialogue.speaker: Tomás
dialogue.spanish: Menos mal, porque si llamamos un taxi a esta hora nos va a salir carísimo con el tráfico.
dialogue.english: Thank goodness, because if we call a taxi at this hour it's going to be super expensive with the traffic.

dialogue.speaker: Julieta
dialogue.spanish: Tal cual. El colectivo sesenta y ocho nos deja a dos cuadras del teatro en quince minutos.
dialogue.english: Totally. The number 68 bus drops us off two blocks from the theater in fifteen minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Tomás
dialogue.spanish: Bárbaro. Carguemos mil pesos en el kiosco y de paso compro unas medialunas para el viaje.
dialogue.english: Awesome. Let's load a thousand pesos at the kiosk and while we're at it I'll buy some croissants for the ride.

questions.question: Why can't Julieta and Tomás take the subway ('el subte') downtown?
options: Line D is closed due to maintenance work
They lost their SUBE transit cards
The station already closed for the night
The train is too crowded to board
questions.explanation: Julieta explains: 'la línea D del subte está cortada por obras' (Line D is closed for maintenance work).

questions.question: Where do they go to add balance to Tomás's SUBE transit card, and which bus will they take?
options: A neighborhood kiosk half a block away, then bus #68
A bank two blocks away, then bus #15
A supermarket across the avenue, then a taxi
They pay the bus driver in cash on bus #40
questions.explanation: Julieta points out a 'kiosco' half a block away on Santa Fe Avenue and says 'El colectivo sesenta y ocho nos deja a dos cuadras del teatro.'

questions.question: How much money does Tomás want to load, and what snack does he mention?
questions.explanation: Tomás says: 'Carguemos mil pesos en el kiosco y de paso compro unas medialunas para el viaje.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: When Tomás exclaims '¡Qué garrón!', what does 'un garrón' mean in Argentine Spanish?
options: A total bummer / drag / piece of bad luck
questions.explanation: In Argentina, '¡Qué garrón!' means 'What a bummer!' or 'What a drag!'
